main_text.l: St. Mary for Travelling; Sebastian and Roch against the Pestilence;
Apollonia against the Toothach; St. Nicholas against Tempests, &c.
Did the Heathen pray to these Daemons for their aid? so do the
Papists to their Saints, as their Breviaries, Rosaries, and Ladies
Psalters testify. Had the Heathen their Feasts, their Statas feriae
to their Daemons? so have the Papists. Had they their Febru-
alia & Proserpinilia with Torches and Lights? so have the Papists
their Candlemas with Lights. Did the Heathen erect Images and
Pillars, or keep the Ashes and Shrines of their Daemons? so do
the Papists: the one had Processions and Adorations, so have the
other; and a great many more things there are wherein Popery
keeps a correspondence with Heathenism. To this purpose you
may read enough in Monsieur de Croy, of the three Conformities.
To make it yet more clear that the corruptions in Religion by
Popery came in by the design of suiting Christian Religion to Pa-
ganism, I shall in a testimony or two shew you that they professedly
avouched the design. Gregory the Great writes chidingly to Se-
renus Bishop of Marseilles (who it seems was no forward Man in
this matter) to this purpose, Thou shouldest have considered that thou
didst converse chiefly with the Gentiles, to whom Pictures are instead of

l.i: Reading, to the end that no offence be given them under colour of law-

main_text.l: ful zeal wherewith thou art not cunningly endued. And in another
Epistle to Mellitus, he adviseth, That the Honours and Offerings

l.i: which the Heathens gave to their Daemons, should be transferred
to the Martyrs, and their Relicks, and gives this reason for it, it
is impossible (saith he) to cut off all at once from stubborn minds.

main_text.l: Eusebius also endeavours to perswade to Christianity
by this Ar-
gument, that the Christians custom of honouring the memories of the

l.i: Martyrs, and solemnly assembling at their Sepulchres, did agree with

main_text.l: the custom of the Gentiles of doing the like honour to their Daemons,
and having mentioned what Hesiod speaks, concerning Plato's
Opinion, that their Champions became Daemons after death,
Helpers and Protectors of Men; for which cause they were wor-
shipped at their Sepulchres as Gods; he adds to this purpose, that

l.i: if these honours had been given to the Favorites of God, and Champions

main_text.l: of true Religion, it had been well enough: and for this shews the
example and custom of Christians then to go to the Tombs of M-
artyrs, there to pray in honour of their blessed Spirits. And
